title: One round trip per row: a page whose work grows with its list

source.ref: Vercel Academy, Next.js Foundations; Prisma ORM's documentation; census H07 (model/spec), R1, S33
source.kind: framework documentation (the framework vendor's course); ORM documentation; model/spec
source.date: Vercel's lesson last updated 2026-08-21 (its page's metadata), read 2026-10-15; Prisma's (ORM v7) read 2026-10-15; the census 2026-09-10
source.says: Vercel's own Next.js course: "Queries inside .map() or for loops are especially problematic", its example one query per user, a hundred users, a hundred queries. Prisma's documentation: "The n+1 problem occurs when looping through query results and performing one additional query per result." Documentation, no incident: the exhibit qualifies by the ADR's fourth kind. The census's own model: one remote lookup per list row; logical data demand should not impose unnecessary serial or per-row round trips (H07). S33 is the overload a multiplied demand causes, not an N+1 incident

claim: ADR-0340 (NEXT 4c's checker): a source read inside a loop over data whose key comes from the loop's element is refused (PW0405), its set read the repair. Before it, none: the census marks H07 'specified but unproven' (batch only with equivalent authorization, consistency, limits and failure semantics; report unbatchable causes)
history: refused, PW0405: a miss the museum found, closed by ADR-0340's checker. The museum's first record (5985fe24, 2026-10-15) showed it a miss, the same change checking clean; ADR-0340 was merged on train-9 the same day, and the exhibit expects the refusal since

repro.how: a price per menu item read in the Server Component with `Promise.all(menu.map(..))`, one round trip each, counted at `/bench/queries`; the repair reads every price in one round trip

pleris.faithful: The same per-item read on the benchmark's store: `Menus.price` per item, `List.map(items, item => Menus.price(item.id))`, inside a public query over the menu. Its neighbour is the store without the change. Until ADR-0340 it checked clean, and the generality corpus held the same shape as a valid neighbour (examples/generality/undeclared_effect/complete-row.pw, which reads by a parameter since). The exhibit's patch is unchanged: the same program, refused now.
